jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
APGA 

Position Summary

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will be responsible for leading the APGA Tour and APGA Foundation next phase of growth and impact. The CEO will be responsible for advancing the organization’s mission, expanding its national influence, strengthening strategic partnerships, driving fundraising efforts, and building a sustainable organization that creates opportunities through golf. The CEO must be equally comfortable presenting in the boardroom, engaging with Fortune 500 executives and major donors, and rolling up their sleeves to support a lean, entrepreneurial organization. The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker who combines executive presence with humility, operational excellence, and an unwavering commitment to the APGA’s mission.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership
Working closely with the Board, develop and execute a long-term strategic vision that advances the APGA mission and organizational growth.
Establish clear priorities and measurable objectives for the organization.
Identify opportunities for innovation, expansion, and increased impact.
Remove organizational obstacles that limit execution and growth.
Inspire confidence among the Board, staff, players, sponsors, donors, and partners.

Organizational Leadership
Build, develop, and retain highly motivated and top-performing team members.
Successfully identify and prioritize opportunities and challenges, keeping the staff and board focused on the highest ROI priorities.
Lead a high-performing, mission-focused team within a lean organizational structure.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Demonstrate a willingness to perform hands-on operational work when needed.
Build systems and processes that support sustainable organizational growth.

Fundraising & Corporate Partnerships
Incorporate innovation and fundraising best practices to support APGA’s growth ambition.
Cultivate and maintain relationships with corporate sponsors and philanthropic partners.
Serve as the organization's primary ambassador with current and prospective supporters.
Identify new revenue opportunities that align with the APGA Tour's mission.

External Relations
Represent the APGA with credibility and professionalism among corporate leaders, community organizations, governing bodies, media, and other stakeholders.
Build strong relationships with senior executives across multiple industries.
Expand partnerships with youth organizations, community organizations, and educational institutions.
Promote the APGA’s nmission and impact nationally.

Financial & Operational Oversight
Oversee the organization's financial health, budgeting, and resource allocation.
Work closely with finance staff and the Board to ensure sound financial stewardship.
Understand financial statements, budgeting, and nonprofit financial management.
Ensure organizational sustainability through disciplined planning and execution.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

Knowledge of:
Knowledge of golf, the golf industry, or a genuine passion for the game and its ability to create opportunity.

Skill in:
Capable of setting long-term organizational direction.
Strategic thinker who translates ideas into actionable plans.
Synthesizes information quickly and makes sound decisions in real time.
Comfortable making difficult decisions while building organizational consensus.
Confident, independent leader who can work collaboratively with founders, board members, and key stakeholders while providing clear direction for the organization's future.
Demonstrated fundraising success, including major gifts and corporate sponsorship development.
Leading a grassroots organization with limited resources.
High intellectual capacity with outstanding analytical and communication skills.
Relationship building; connects naturally with corporate executives, donors, community leaders, and players.
Resilient, adaptable, and resourceful in a fast-paced environment.
High integrity and unquestioned ethical standards.

Ability to:
Inspire confidence across diverse audiences.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will possess many of the following qualities:
Experience
Senior leadership experience within a nonprofit organization, mission-driven enterprise, or college athletics.
P&L responsibility for $3+ million annual budgets.
Experience leading a team of 5 direct reports.
Experience working with Boards of Directors and executive leadership teams.
Strong understanding of financial management and organizational budgeting.
Experience building strategic partnerships across the corporate, nonprofit, and community sectors.

Travel

25-30% of the time, Various locations, mostly US

$180,000 - $200,00 per year + Bonus + Optional healthcare

CLIENT SUMMARY

MinistrySafe is a faith-driven abuse prevention organization dedicated to protecting children and vulnerable individuals through training, background checks, and preventative systems designed specifically for churches, ministries, camps, schools, and child-serving organizations.
Founded approximately 20 years ago by attorneys Gregory Love (CEO) and Kimberlee Norris (Chief Legal Officer), MinistrySafe was created after representing victims of child abuse and recognizing the need for proactive prevention rather than reactive legal representation. Today, the organization serves more than 25,000 customers nationwide and continues to experience strong year-over-year growth.

The company’s primary services include abuse awareness training and comprehensive background checks, with a strong emphasis on education and prevention as the most effective tools for protecting children. While MinistrySafe primarily serves churches and ministry organizations, it also operates a secular-facing division called Abuse Prevention Systems (APS), serving schools, camps, nonprofits, and other child-serving entities.

The organization is deeply mission-driven, and highly relational in culture. Leadership values integrity, stewardship, strong communication, and entrepreneurial thinking.

POSITION OBJECTIVE

MinistrySafe is hiring a Director of Partnerships to work with the CEO to expand strategic partnerships, strengthen enterprise relationships, cultivate new markets, and drive organizational growth. This highly relational, externally focused leader will manage and grow key partnerships across churches, denominations, insurance providers, ministries, educational organizations, and other child-serving institutions.

The Director will focus on preserving existing partnerships and identifying new growth opportunities. This role requires an entrepreneurial, mission-aligned leader who understands church culture, communicates effectively with ministry leaders, and can execute with strategic vision.

Collaborate with internal leadership to support growth initiatives and strategic expansion efforts
Stay informed on legal, regulatory, and industry developments related to child safety and abuse prevention

new_jobs.title: Assistant Director of Institutional Giving, Corporate Membership
new_jobs.description:
The Museum of Modern Art ('MoMA’) is currently accepting applications for an Assistant Director of Institutional Giving, Corporate Membership who will be responsible for managing a multi-tier corporate membership program for MoMA, including stewardship and ongoing solicitation of corporate members and donors around MoMA exhibitions and programs.
Responsibilities:

Responsible for stewardship and ongoing solicitation of corporate members.
Develops and implements annual and long-term Corporate Membership strategy and goals to identify, cultivate, and solicit prospects to expand corporate membership.
As the main point of contact for the MoMA Corporate Membership program, ensures a positive onboarding experience, warm ongoing communication, and retention of Corporate Member companies.  Conducts ongoing stewardship, including in-person meetings, tours, and visits.
Works with Trustees, Individual Philanthropy, Corporate Partnership, and Foundation teams to identify new Corporate Membership prospects and strengthen donor relationships across the Department.
Coordinates barters and in-kind agreements related to Marketing and Audience Strategy, Communications, Retail, Special Events, IT, and other departments as needed.
Collaborates with colleagues in curatorial, Communications, Marketing and Audience Strategy, Membership, Retail, Special Events, and other areas to keep donors informed about Museum exhibitions and programs.
Generates regular and ad hoc reports and communications to assist donors in assessing the use of their benefits, impressions gained, and overall return on marketing investment.
Actively works to present upsell opportunities to donors around Corporate Membership upgrades, Museum benefit tickets and tables, corporate entertaining, retail purchases and licensing, gift membership, and exhibition and program sponsorship.
Greets and escorts VIPs as needed.
Participates in recruitment for select open positions and makes hiring recommendations or decisions for staff vacancies; supervises assigned staff on daily basis, providing relevant training, feedback, guidance, professional development, etc.; ensures compliance with and comprehension of Museum policies and relevant collective bargaining agreement, if applicable; conducts annual performance reviews with direct staff; manages the constructive discipline process, as warranted; etc.
Performs any other duties reasonably related to the functions described above.

Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree and five to 10 years of progressively responsible corporate and/or sponsorship fundraising experience, including donor portfolio management and staff management.
Passion for modern and contemporary art.
Superior interpersonal/verbal and written communications, professional negotiating skills, and diplomacy.
Superior organizational and project management skills, with ability to work independently and proactively under strict deadlines.
Ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously with keen attention to detail.
Aptitude with budgets and financial documentation.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Salesforce or other CRM database systems.
Proficiency in at least one language, in addition to English, is preferred.
On-site presence is required five days a week during the 90-day initial employment period.  Thereafter the schedule is four days per week onsite, subject to change at management’s discretion, with the understanding that some weeks on-site presence five days a week will be required.

Reports to: 
Acting Director of Institutional Giving
Supervises: 
Development Assistant
Salary range: 
Minimum of $120,000 to maximum of $135,000 per annum
